note: General first-aid guidance for bystanders. Not a diagnosis. India emergency numbers: 112 (all emergencies), 108 (ambulance), 101 (fire), 100 (police).

protocols.title: Make the scene safe
steps: Stay out of traffic. Switch on hazard lights.
Switch off damaged vehicle engines. No smoking or flames.
Send someone to wave traffic down or place a warning.
Do not move injured people unless fire or danger is near.
Keep your phone free for the ambulance call-back.
dont: Don't remove a helmet.
Don't give food or water.

protocols.title: Not breathing - start CPR
steps: Call 112 or 108 now. Put the phone on speaker.
Lay the person flat on their back on a hard surface.
Heel of one hand on the centre of the chest, other hand on top.
Push hard and fast: 5-6 cm deep, 100-120 times a minute.
Do not stop until the ambulance team or an AED takes over.
If an AED is nearby, send someone to get it and follow its voice.
dont: Don't stop to check the pulse again and again.

protocols.title: Unconscious person
steps: Call 112 or 108 now.
Tap shoulders and shout. No response? Check breathing for 10 seconds.
Breathing normally: roll onto their side, tilt head back gently.
Not breathing normally: start chest compressions (tap 'Not breathing').
Stay with them and watch breathing until help arrives.
dont: Don't give water, food or medicine.
Don't move them if neck injury is possible - unless breathing is blocked.

protocols.title: Heavy bleeding
steps: Press firmly on the wound with a clean cloth. Use your hand if you have no cloth.
Keep pressing hard. Do not lift to look.
Blood soaks through? Add more cloth on top and keep pressing.
Raise the injured arm or leg if no broken bone is suspected.
Lay the person down and keep them warm.
dont: Don't remove cloth that is stuck or soaked - add more on top.
Don't pull out objects stuck in the wound.

protocols.title: Choking
steps: Ask: 'Are you choking?' If they cannot speak or cough, act now.
Lean them forward. Give 5 firm back blows between the shoulder blades.
Then 5 abdominal thrusts: fist above the navel, pull in and up.
Repeat 5 and 5 until it comes out or they collapse.
If they collapse: call 112 and start CPR.
dont: Don't do blind finger sweeps.
Infants: back blows and chest thrusts only - no belly thrusts.

protocols.title: Burns
steps: Move away from fire or heat. Stop the burning: smother flames with a blanket.
Cool the burn under cool running water for 20 minutes.
Take off rings, watches and loose clothing near it - not if stuck to skin.
Cover loosely with clean cling film or a non-fluffy cloth.
Chemical burn: keep rinsing with water until help arrives.
dont: Don't use ice, butter, toothpaste or oil.
Don't burst blisters.

protocols.title: Broken bone
steps: Keep the person still. Support the injured part in the position found.
Splint with a rolled newspaper or stick, padded with cloth, if help is delayed.
Bone through the skin: cover with a clean cloth. Press around it, not on it.
Place a wrapped ice pack on the area. Never ice directly on skin.
Watch for pale, cold or numb fingers or toes.
dont: Don't straighten the limb.
Don't let them eat or drink - they may need surgery.

protocols.title: Head, neck or back injury
steps: Call 112 or 108. Tell them it is a head, neck or spine injury.
Keep the person completely still. Hold their head steady with both hands.
Tell them not to move or shake their head.
Watch breathing and responsiveness. Be ready to start CPR.
Bleeding from the scalp: press gently around the wound.
dont: Don't move them unless fire or danger is near.
Don't remove a helmet.

protocols.title: Chest pain or trouble breathing
steps: Call 112 or 108 now.
Sit them down in the position that makes breathing easiest. Loosen tight clothes.
Keep them calm and still. Do not let them walk.
Pain is NOT from an injury and they are awake, not allergic: they may chew one 300 mg aspirin.
If they collapse and stop breathing: start CPR.
dont: Don't give aspirin if there is bleeding or an injury.
Don't give food or drink.

protocols.title: Shock (pale, cold, clammy)
steps: Call 112 or 108.
Lay them down. Raise legs about 30 cm - not if head, spine or leg is injured.
Cover with a blanket or jacket. Keep them warm.
Stop any visible bleeding by pressing on it.
Talk calmly. Keep checking breathing.
dont: Don't give food or drink.
Don't let them sit up or walk.

protocols.title: Seizure / fits
steps: Clear hard objects away. Put something soft under their head.
Note the time. Loosen tight clothing around the neck.
Let it run its course. Stay with them.
When shaking stops, roll them onto their side.
Call 112 if it lasts over 5 minutes, repeats, or they are injured or pregnant.
dont: Don't hold them down.
Don't put anything in their mouth.

protocols.title: Electric shock
steps: Do NOT touch them while they may be live.
Switch off the power at the main switch if you can.
Otherwise push the wire away with a dry wooden stick or dry plastic.
Call 112 or 108. Check breathing. Start CPR if needed.
Cover any burns loosely with a clean cloth.
dont: Don't use anything wet or metal.
Don't go near high-voltage lines - wait for the power company.

protocols.title: Eye injury
steps: Don't rub the eye.
Chemical splash: rinse with clean running water for 15 minutes.
Object stuck in the eye: leave it. Cover loosely with a clean cup or pad.
Cover the other eye too to limit movement.
Get medical help.
dont: Don't press on the eye.
Don't pull out stuck objects.

protocols.title: Minor cut or scrape
steps: Wash your hands. Press a clean cloth on the cut for a few minutes to stop bleeding.
Rinse the wound under clean running water. Remove loose dirt.
Apply antiseptic and cover with a clean dressing.
Change the dressing daily. Watch for redness, pus, swelling or fever.
Ask a doctor about a tetanus shot if you haven't had one in 5-10 years.
dont: Don't use turmeric, soil or ash on the wound.
Don't keep pressing a bleed that won't stop - get help.

protocols.title: Bruise or sprain
steps: Rest the area. Stop using it.
Wrapped ice pack for 15-20 minutes, every 2-3 hours.
Snug (not tight) bandage for support.
Raise the limb above heart level when resting.
See a doctor if you can't put weight on it, it looks bent, or fingers or toes go numb.
dont: Don't put ice directly on skin.
Don't massage a fresh injury.

protocols.title: Nosebleed
steps: Sit up and lean forward.
Pinch the soft part of the nose firmly for 10 minutes without letting go.
Breathe through your mouth. Spit out any blood.
Still bleeding after 20 minutes, or it followed a hit to the head: go to a hospital.
dont: Don't tilt the head back.
Don't blow your nose for several hours.

protocols.title: Small minor burn
steps: Cool under cool running water for 20 minutes.
Remove rings or watches nearby before it swells.
Cover loosely with clean cling film or a non-stick dressing.
Go to a hospital if bigger than your palm, on the face, hands or joints, or blistering badly.
dont: Don't use ice, butter or toothpaste.
Don't burst blisters.
